notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Black plates with white text; military ones show a small flag on the left.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Most coverage has an escort follow car, sometimes ahead or far behind the Street View car, in several different models.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: The Google car is black with a medium-length thin antenna, though the colour is not always visible.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Neat rows of olive trees on raked, weed-free soil often line the roads.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Road lines are usually white and outer lines can be dashed or solid; a few roads in one big southern city have yellow centre lines.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Bilingual signs are common, pairing a script of lines and dots with Latin letters. Direction signs are white with a distinctive Latin font.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Doors, windows and gates are often painted a specific traditional blue, especially on the island of Djerba.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Red and white striped curbs are common.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: White concrete markers with a rounded red, yellow or green top show distances to the nearest towns and the road number on the road side.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: A fairly unique stop sign with text in two scripts; similar ones exist in two other countries, while another uses a hand symbol.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the right.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: Coverage is mostly on the east coast, from Bizerte in the north to Medenine in the south, in bigger towns and on main roads.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A light green Toyota follow car is seen across the far north and never south of Hammamet.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: The most common follow car is a dark green Mazda with a military plate with a red strip on the left, from Hammamet down to Djerba.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: The central-northern holy city has a unique white Mitsubishi follow car with white mirrors.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Djerba is usually without a follow car, with many palms and whitewashed buildings with blue doors and windows.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: North of the capital is hilly, Mediterranean and agricultural, with fields mostly fallow when captured.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Between Hammamet and Gabes it is very flat and arid, growing drier southwards; south of Gabes it turns desert-like.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A lake with teal water, flat shores and slight hills to its south marks the far north.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: A large concentration of palm trees in one place points to Gabes.
